title: Consolidate entity IDs and migrate varchar primary keys to UUIDs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: The control plane schema currently uses a mix of opaque varchar primary keys (legacy external IDs, concatenated tokens) and integer sequences. This has created inconsistent join performance and prevents use of partitioning, pg_repack, and some newer index types. Goal: Migrate core entity tables (organizations, projects, routes, deployments) to native UUID primary keys, remove redundant varchar PKs, and consolidate FK relationships. This reduces row width, enables compact btree indexes, and simplifies sharding/replication paths. Scope: - Add UUID columns and backfill in a safe, transactional and reversible way - Introduce FK UUID references alongside existing varchar FKs - Gradual cutover for services to write/read UUIDs, then drop old columns and convert indexes - Add/adjust indexes where needed (partial, expression, covering) - Run VACUUM/ANALYZE and observe query plans Postgres version targeted: 14+ (ensure contrib extensions available).
acceptance_criteria: All identified tables have non-null UUID column populated and validated against existing varchar PK mapping
No customer-facing errors or increased 95th latency beyond 10% during migration windows
All services can toggle between varchar PKs and UUIDs via feature flags with zero downtime rollout
Query plans for top-20 control-plane endpoints show no regressions; targeted slow queries improve by at least 15% after index tuning
Old varchar PK columns and deprecated indexes removed in a follow-up cleanup PR within release window
migration_plan: Phase 0: Prep - audit tables, collect row counts, identify hot queries and dependent materialized views
Phase 1: Add nullable uuid columns with default gen_random_uuid() in a single ALTER statement per table (non-blocking in PG14+ with concurrent schema changes policy)
Phase 2: Backfill in batches using idempotent worker job: select ranges by primary key, update uuid column, commit per chunk (chunk size tuned per table)
Phase 3: Create new indexes on uuid columns concurrently, add FK constraints as NOT VALID to avoid long locks
Phase 4: Switch services behind feature flags to write/read uuid columns; run integration tests and canary traffic
Phase 5: Mark FK constraints VALID, monitor, then deprecate varchar PK usage across codebase
Phase 6: Drop varchar PK columns and redundant indexes in a maintenance window; run VACUUM FULL or pg_repack where needed
rollback_plan: Any phase should be reversible by toggling feature flags to continue using varchar PKs
If backfill stress causes high load, pause backfill workers and resume with smaller chunk sizes
If a new index or FK causes lock contention, drop or set constraint NOT VALID and revert to prior index configuration
Last-resort: restore from logical replication slot snapshot taken immediately before destructive drops (documented and tested in staging)
performance_testing: Load test backfill worker with synthetic payload at 2x expected production write rate and monitor CPU, wal_bytes, replication lag
Run explain analyze on top-20 queries before/after index addition; record planning and execution time changes
Smoke test API endpoints for 95th percentile latency across normal and cold cache scenarios
Track metrics: db.cpu_seconds, db.tx_per_sec, db.long_queries, wal_write_bytes, replication_lag, control_plane_api_95th_latency
notes: We will avoid making PK name changes visible to clients; a mapping table will exist for legacy external IDs.
Expectation: index size reduction ~10-30% on wide tables due to uuid vs varchar savings and removal of collation overhead.
Coordination: schedule with infra team to increase WAL retention during backfills and inform SRE on replication lag thresholds.
